hypotheses.mechanism: The scorer matches each frame on its own. It maximises the sum of 1/(1+d) within 7 um (tracksdata DistanceMatching, optimal) and ignores edges. With sparse GT, each annotated node is therefore matched to the predicted node NEAREST to it. Recomputed on exp39: 1,410 of the 6,732 FN (21%) are 'theft' cases. In each one our track's actual successor y lies within 7 um of GT v, but another predicted node is closer and takes the match. 588 of them have a margin under 1 um and 909 under 2 um. Each such case costs 1 FN plus 1 FP, because the source is annotated and y is unmatched. Localisation decides these near-ties. Our pipeline computes float coordinates (linefit smoothing, weight 0.8), but write_test_submission then writes int(round()). That adds rounding noise on a 1.625 um z grid (RMS 0.47 um) and 0.41 um in xy. The x138 notebook also rounds at output (its line ~3836), so the port we are doing keeps this loss. It also quantises away most of the V1284 head's sub-voxel z correction. The public royerlab csv_to_geffs.py reads the CSV and casts z,y,x to pl.Float64, so float coordinates are accepted by the converter.
hypotheses.change: In write_test_submission (and write_geff in the lab), write z,y,x as floats rounded to 3 decimals, clipped at >= 0, instead of int(round()). Topology and node count are unchanged. Second step: with floats reaching the scorer, re-run the linefit grid (weight 0.6/0.8/1.0 x window 2/3). B28 tuned it with rounded output, where sub-voxel smoothing was destroyed. Apply on top of the x138-head port so the head's z correction survives.
hypotheses.upper_bound: Measured already, not estimated. I reimplemented the official edge scoring (per-frame optimal matching plus the FP rules). It reproduces the official exp39 TP/FP/FN exactly in 199/199 videos with rounded coordinates. With float coordinates: adj 0.90244 -> 0.90422 = +0.0018 over all 199 videos. 44b6: +0.0020. 6bba: +0.0018. dTP +70, dFP -190, dFN -70. Videos better/worse: 73/47. z-float only: +0.0010. Ceiling of the theft class: 1,410 x (1 + 0.9) x 7.4e-6 = 0.020, most of which only better detection can reach. A float-aware smoother retune could plausibly add +0.0005..0.001.
hypotheses.lab_test: Script: scratchpad roundall.py (reads the exp39 tail npz and the GT geff; about 75 s for 199 videos). The same switch goes in replay.write_geff (a rounding flag). Run SELECTION, then one CONFIRMATION, then the linefit grid with floats. Success: >= +0.0015 on confirmation, both embryos > 0, node count identical. Then check that the submission CSV with float columns parses on Kaggle, bundled with the next probe.
hypotheses.expected_gain: Local +0.0018 measured (+0.002..0.003 with a smoother retune). Public: +0.001..0.002. The public multiplier is identical (same nodes), so the J part carries over: 0.9 x (+0.0020 J-relative) ~ +0.0018. That is below the +-0.003 single-probe noise, so ship it inside a bundle.
hypotheses.transfer_risk: Low. No nodes change, no network output is trusted more, and the gain comes from removing an independent quantisation noise. Residual risks: (1) Kaggle's server-side converter may differ from the public csv_to_geffs.py. The worst case is a parse error, which shows up as a failed submission rather than a silent loss. (2) Truncation instead of rounding would hurt, so verify on the first probe that the score does not drop more than 0.003.
hypotheses.not_closed_because: This is not a detector, TTA or relink change. The x138 port keeps int(round()) at output. B28 swept linefit only with rounded output. Eric's sub-voxel peak refinement (-0.002 LB) changed detector peaks; this changes only output quantisation of already smoothed coordinates.

hypotheses.mechanism: In 6bba, 909 transitions are exact duplicate frames (more than 80% of predicted edges have zero length). They occur in 114 of 128 videos, mostly single frames (740 runs of 1, 17 of 2, 45 of 3). 44b6 has none. The GT ALSO freezes: its step on frozen transitions has median 0. So the transition AFTER a freeze is a real 2-4 frame step. The GT step there has median 3.37 um and p90 7.8 um, and 13.8% exceed 7 um, against 1.86 / 4.16 / 1.7% normally. These transitions hold 36% of all 6bba GT edges longer than 7 um, which is much of the swap class (median 9.3 um). The motion relink predicts from the last velocity. That velocity is zero across the duplicate, and the gates are tuned for one step. Measured on exp39, 6bba, post-freeze transitions against normal ones: FP per 1k TP 178 vs 47.6. FN rate 13.3% vs 4.8% (858 FN; 462 wrong successor, 195 track ends, 201 unmatched). The edge filter already drops 487 of the 995 post-freeze FP. After it, 508 FP remain against about 202 expected at the normal rate. Global translation on post-freeze transitions is the same as normal (1.10 vs 1.07 um); the residual motion is larger. So this is doubled cell motion, not drift, and gshift cannot fix it.
hypotheses.change: Post-processing only. In the kernel, detect duplicate frames exactly: np.array_equal of consecutive raw frames, or identical detection sets. For the transition t+k -> t+k+1 after a freeze run of length k: (1) the motion relink predicts x + (k+1)*v, with v from the last non-frozen step (x_t - x_{t-1}), and scales the tight/relaxed gates (5.5/10 um) by sqrt(k+1) to (k+1)/2 (grid). (2) Scale the gap-closing / stitch radius and the safe-division parent/sister gates the same way; 13 of 125 6bba GT divisions fall on post-freeze transitions. (3) Make linefit use real time: collapse each duplicate onto its twin so the fit does not bend the double step (weight 0.8 moves a frozen node by about 0.64 of a step). The edge filter keeps running afterwards. On 44b6 the rule is an exact no-op, which gives a built-in control.
hypotheses.upper_bound: Oracle against exp39: excess FN 548 x 7.4e-6 + excess FP 729 x 0.9 x 7.4e-6 = 0.0041 + 0.0048 = +0.0089 local (6bba only). Against exp39+ef: about (306 FP x 0.9 + ~450 FN) x 7.4e-6 ~ +0.005. A 2-step motion model realistically recovers 30-60%.
hypotheses.lab_test: Implement as a relink/tail patch in the replay (relink_rerun already exists in edge_anatomy/anatomy.py). Run on SELECTION (6bba), then one CONFIRMATION run. Read the results out by transition class (normal / frozen / post) using the parquet columns t and len_pre_um. Success: excess post-freeze FN+FP cut by >= 40%, normal-transition delta within +-0.0003, 44b6 bit-identical, 6bba confirmation >= +0.0015 with CI > 0. The protocol's rule 'each embryo >= +0.001' must be replaced by '44b6 identical', or it rejects the rule by construction.
hypotheses.expected_gain: Local +0.0015..0.003 on all 199 videos (6bba is 84% of the D weight), 0 on 44b6. Public or private: the same, multiplied by P(hidden embryo has duplicate frames). 6bba has them in 89% of videos, so the prior is about 0.5 for a same-rig embryo. Expected public +0.000..0.003.
hypotheses.transfer_risk: Asymmetric and low. If the hidden embryos have no duplicate frames, the rule never fires: zero gain, zero loss. It trusts no network output, since it only changes geometry and gates at an exactly detectable data defect. Main risk: overfitting the gate scale on 6bba. Mitigate by picking it on SELECTION only, with at most 3 values.
hypotheses.not_closed_because: A16 looked only at detections ('identical input => identical detections; no rule needed') and never at the transition after a freeze. The closed relink knobs, flow prior and gshift are global settings or translation corrections; this is a conditional motion model for a data defect whose errors are measured at 3.7x the normal FP rate.

hypotheses.mechanism: Under the official FP rule, an edge costs something only when an endpoint matches an annotated node. Adding an edge therefore pays exactly when P(correct | evaluable) > J/(1+J) = 0.474. Deleting a node pays only if P(it carries a TP) is below 0.1*J*D/N_est: 0.0007 TP-edge units on 44b6 and 0.0089 on 6bba (GT nodes are 0.77% vs 5.4% of N_est). So end->start stitching is almost free where nothing is annotated, and it adds no nodes. On the ef graph, the ILP-edge stitch adds 7,182 edges. 96% of them are non-evaluable; the evaluable ones are 281 TP / 19 FP (0.937, far above 0.474). Confirmation: +0.0021 (44b6 +0.0012, 6bba +0.0025). It failed only the rule 'gains on >= 55% of 44b6 videos' (0.15). That criterion is structurally unreachable on 44b6: most of its videos have zero changed evaluable edges and hence a delta of exactly 0. The same FN census gives 854 FN where u is a track end while GT v is matched (195 at post-freeze transitions), and 624 FN (a_tail) where the short-track filter or pruning removed an annotated node. Stitching BEFORE the tail turns some sub-6-frame fragments into long tracks, so they survive.
hypotheses.change: Move stitch_final_graph (ILP-edge condition; variant st_p07: p >= 0.7, 240 TP / 8 FP) in front of filter_short_track_components, with gate doubling on post-freeze transitions. Replace the per-video gate with an evaluability-conditioned one: among videos where >= 1 evaluable edge changed, >= 55% gain per embryo, plus a per-embryo bootstrap CI and a J-vs-multiplier split (reject if more than 70% of the gain is multiplier, per zhincez).
hypotheses.upper_bound: b_break oracle +0.003 plus a_tail 624 x 7.4e-6 = +0.0046, so about +0.0076. Measured after-tail version: +0.0020..0.0021. Node-cost check: rescuing R fragment nodes costs ~0.009 x R/1000 TP-edge equivalents on 6bba, so 5,000 rescued nodes cost about 45 TP-edges, i.e. -0.0003.
hypotheses.lab_test: Replay with --patch stitch placed before the tail; SELECTION, then one CONFIRMATION run. Read out added TP/FP, rescued nodes, the multiplier share, and the evaluability-conditioned per-video fraction for each embryo. Success: >= +0.002 on confirmation, CI > 0 in each embryo, >= 55% of affected videos gain.
hypotheses.expected_gain: Local +0.002..0.003. Public +0.001..0.002. Even if test precision halves to 0.6, the gain keeps (0.6 x 1.9 - 0.9)/(0.937 x 1.9 - 0.9) = 27%.
hypotheses.transfer_risk: Medium-low. It trusts the ILP edge, which is in-sample, but only where the relink left BOTH ends free (no competition), and the break-even precision is 0.47 against 0.94 locally. Rescued fragments add nodes; keep only fragments that join a track of >= 6 frames, so the node count stays within +0.1%.
hypotheses.not_closed_because: The stitch was measured (+0.002, both embryos positive) but never probed. It was rejected by a gate artefact of sparse 44b6 annotation, not by a negative delta. Placing it before the tail is new. Min-track-length changes (closed) alter the node count; this does not.

hypotheses.mechanism: I split the edge filter's drops by transition class, using a label-free flag: the median step of the network-scored relink_ilp_tight edges > 3.5 um, or post-freeze. Of the ~1,904 FP that ef removes, 1,235 fall on large-step transitions and 487 on post-freeze ones. Only 181 FP (with 120 TP lost) fall on normal transitions, which carry 82% of the edges. Net on normal transitions: 181 x 0.9 - 120 ~ +43 TP-edges ~ +0.0003. The large-step transitions are mostly global drift: the median displacement vector is 2.73 um against a 1.42 um residual. They hold 29% of all FP in 11% of edges; the 44b6 ones reach 300-1,800 FP per 1k TP. So about 90% of ef's +0.0162 is repair of anomalous transitions, not trust in the in-sample ILP on ordinary steps. Probe 29 therefore mostly measures whether the PUBLIC embryo has drift jumps or freezes. gshift being neutral on the LB hints it may have few, while the private embryos (71%) may well have them.
hypotheses.change: (1) Build ef_anom: apply ef only on flagged transitions. Flags: post-freeze by exact duplicate detection, or ILP-tight median step >= 1.8x the video's median transition step (relative, so it carries to faster or slower embryos). This removes the only part of ef that depends on in-sample ILP trust. (2) Finals policy: if probe 29 lands flat on the public board (within +-0.002), keep ef_anom in one final anyway, because the rule is near-neutral on ordinary transitions. Drop it only if the public result is negative beyond noise (<= -0.003).
hypotheses.upper_bound: Local: ef's +0.0162 on confirmation; ef_anom should keep >= 90% of it (+0.0146), since 1,722 of the ~1,904 removed FP are on flagged transitions. Private upside: +0.000..0.016, scaled by the anomaly rate of the hidden embryos. Public: the same logic for the one public embryo.
hypotheses.lab_test: Replay ef and ef_anom on CONFIRMATION with a per-transition-class readout (normal / big / post-freeze / frozen), plus a sensitivity check of the relative flag at 1.5x / 1.8x / 2.2x. Success: ef_anom >= 0.9 x ef, normal-transition delta within +-0.0005, and the flag fires on <= 15% of transitions per video. Also log flag counts in the kernel on the 4 dummy test clips (train copies) to verify it fires identically in the kernel.
hypotheses.expected_gain: Mainly protection plus private upside: a rule worth +0.016 locally is not thrown away because of one public embryo. Expected private gain 0.3-0.6 x 0.0146 ~ +0.004..0.009 if the hidden embryos resemble train in anomaly rate. Public: +0.000..0.015, read from probe 29.
hypotheses.transfer_risk: The anomaly flag may fire differently on embryos with other motion speeds, which is why the threshold is relative to each video's own median step. If probe 29 is clearly negative, ef harms ordinary transitions on test and ef_anom should also be dropped.
hypotheses.not_closed_because: The edge filter is being probed and is not closed. gshift (closed) was a translation correction inside the relink; this keeps the already validated drop rule and restricts it to label-free anomalous transitions, plus a decision rule for the finals. The attribution itself is new.
